messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: HIGH - alb-targets-unhealthy-eu-west-1 fired for service: api-public (pg: prod-eu) :rotating_light:
pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident #INC-2219 created and triggered P1 page to oncall (alex).
alex: ack'd. i'm on it, pinging datadog + cloudwatch now. tagging @net-eng in case ALB/dns is flapping.
sara: saw spikes in 5xx from eu endpoints in dashboard, looks like TLS handshake errors in front of the alb: 'TLS alert, handshake failure' in logs. linking logs: https://dd.app/xyz/alerts
noah: also seeing TargetGroup health dropping to 0/4 on the eu-prod-app tg. connection reset from several ips.
alex: can someone run `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:...` and paste results? want to confirm reason codes.
jamie: paste from cloud shell:
```
{ "TargetsHealthDescriptions": [ { "Target": { "Id": "10.0.12.7","Port": 8080 }, "HealthCheckPort": "8080", "TargetHealth": { "State": "unhealthy", "Reason": "HTTP-5XX" } }, { "Target": { "Id": "10.0.12.8","Port": 8080 }, "TargetHealth": { "State": "unhealthy", "Reason": "TLS-ALERT" } } ] }
```
alex: ok two classes: some nodes returning 5xx, some failing TLS handshake. did we rollout a new cert or nginx change in eu last night?
sara: we rotated app certs in eu for mTLS test at 02:10 UTC but rollback job showed success. curious. linking deploy logs: https://ci/reports/789
noah: i'm running `curl -v https://api.eu.redwood.example/health` from inside the VPC via bastion — handshake fails with `alert handshake failure` against 10.0.12.7:8080 forwarded through alb.
net-eng: seeing increased SYN_RECV and some RSTs at the ALB. not a pure linux drop; could be cipher mismatch. what ciphers are the app processes advertising?
jamie: app nginx conf shows `ssl_ciphers TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` — should be compatible. app/container image unchanged since last week.
alex: plan: 1) remove unhealthy targets from TG to stop failed handshakes, 2) shift small % of traffic to us-west as emergency failover, 3) roll one eu instance with debug enabled to check cert chain and SNI.
sara: +1. i'll open a quick routing override in Route53 health checks if we need DNS failover. TTL is 60s so should move quickly.
noah: i'm on step 1 — deregistering targets now `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=10.0.12.7`
infra-bot: Notice: Deregistration initiated for target 10.0.12.7 in prod-eu (draining connections).
alex: good. once 2/4 gone we'll monitor 5xx rate. paging policy: if still >1% errors after 2min escalate to net-eng lead and hit emergency failover.
net-eng: starting deeper packet capture on the ALB-fronting subnets, also checking cert on the ALB listener. not seeing any cert updates in control plane logs.
jamie: traffic dropped ~70% errors after removing two bad targets. still seeing intermittent TLS failures but magnitude down.
sara: i'm pre-staging a Route53 failover record pointing to us-west. not flipping yet. if errors bounce back we'll flip and alert customers.
alex: notif to support: posting ETA and initial impact: "Partial API failures for EU customers, ~40% errors at peak, degraded for 2xx endpoints that hit unhealthy targets. We have mitigations in progress." @support please hold customer-facing comms until we confirm failover. :email:
noah: in parallel i'm spinning a fresh eu instance with debug cert pipeline and running `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.12.9:8080 -servername api.eu.redwood.example` to inspect chain.
noah: result: server sends only TLS1.2 ciphers and missing intermediate cert in chain for some instances — looks like leftover cert bundle from older deploy.
alex: bingo. that explains handshake failures for clients expecting TLS1.3. rollback option: revert cert bundle to previous full-chain across the ASG, or rotate to a known-good cert. which is faster?
jamie: we have an automated cert deploy job; rolling it to previous bundle takes ~3min per instance. manual restart of affected pods with mounted full-chain available would be ~5-7min but less risk.
sara: recommend: do instance-level restart with known-good chain on 2 instances first, monitor, then do the rest if green. if not green within 10min, flip DNS failover to us-west.
alex: agreed. noah/team proceed with restarts. net-eng stand by for packet capture while we confirm chain. i'll update PD incident timeline and escalation.
pagerduty: Note: Incident #INC-2219 acknowledged by alex. Escalation to on-call lead in 12 minutes if not resolved.
noah: restarted 2 pods with full-chain. health checks are green on those. overall error rate dropped to 0.9%.
jamie: pushing restart across remaining hosts now in waves to avoid capacity drop.
alex: excellent. we'll keep this thread for live comms. after final host restarted and 0.3% error sustained for 10 minutes we'll close the PD and file for RCA. handoff: i'm oncall for next 30 minutes then sara will take follow-up for postmortem.
net-eng: capture logs show TLS server hello from instances missing intermediate CA. evidence collected.
sara: starting a short incident summary for internal and flagged for support. customers.csv list shows 3 enterprise customers in eu saw errors; we'll prep outreach if they require it.
alex: closing actions (to collect): 1) root cause: bad cert bundle during cert rotation job, 2) mitigation: restarted pods with good chain, 3) preventive: add post-deploy cert chain validator in CI, 4) ops doc update for emergency DNS failover.
jamie: noted, i'll create the PD timeline + attach captures.
alex: thanks all — transitioning to monitoring mode. if anything spikes re-open thread. :thumbsup:
